prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on the Salt Lake Temple, the granite temple in the heart of Salt Lake City that took 40 years to build.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple pages, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Brigham Young chose the temple site in July 1847, days after the pioneers reached the valley, and ground was broken in February 1853. The temple took 40 years to build and was dedicated in April 1893 by President Wilford Woodruff.

prompts.display_text: Pin a land whose very first convert was baptized between 1870 and 1899.
prompts.text_original: A country or territory where the first known convert was baptized between 1870 and 1899.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: While the Saints were still settling the West, missionaries opened new lands. Finland, Mexico, Austria, Belgium, Samoa, American Samoa and Tonga all saw their first known convert baptisms between 1876 and 1892.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: In 1877 Meliton Trejo and Louis Garff baptized Jose Epifanio Jesus at Hermosillo, the first convert in Mexico.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: In 1892 Alipate, the first Tongan convert, was baptized and confirmed by Brigham Smoot at Mu‘a.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: In 1889 Ifopa of Sale‘imoa village became the first convert baptized on Upolu.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: In 1888 Malaea, on Aunu‘u, became the first convert baptized after the Samoan Mission opened.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: In 1883 Paul Haslinger became the first convert baptized in Austria, at Lambach.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: In 1888 Henrietta Esselmann and her son Frederick Pieper were the first baptized in Belgium, at Antwerp.

answers.name: Finland
answers.fact: In 1876 Johanna Charlotta Berg became the first convert baptized in Finland, at Vaasa.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the USA whose Church story has a chapter set in Nauvoo, Illinois.
prompts.text_original: A country outside the United States whose Church story includes a chapter that took place in Nauvoo, Illinois (1839-1846).
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Nauvoo was a launching point for the worldwide Church. A Welshman was baptized in the Mississippi there, a Dane began translating scripture while guarding the temple, Norwegians nearby joined, missionaries left for the Pacific, a mission to Russia was called, and leaders planned a move toward Mexican territory.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Dan Jones, a native of Wales, was baptized in the Mississippi River at Nauvoo in 1843.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: In 1845 Peter Olsen Hansen began translating the Book of Mormon into Danish while serving as a guard in the Nauvoo Temple.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: In 1844 Joseph Smith and the Apostles in Nauvoo began planning an expedition to seek a new home, possibly in Mexican territory.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: In the 1840s several Norwegians living near Nauvoo joined the Church.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: In 1843 Addison Pratt and three companions were set apart in Nauvoo; they ended up preaching on Tubuai in 1844.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: In 1843 Joseph Smith in Nauvoo called Orson Hyde and George J. Adams on a mission to Russia, which never took place.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Elder Ezra Taft Benson brought postwar relief to the Saints in 1946.
prompts.text_original: A country where Ezra Taft Benson, as European Mission president in 1946, visited Saints or directed postwar relief after World War II.
prompts.citation: Church History Department, Global Histories country chronologies, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: After World War II, Elder Ezra Taft Benson spent 1946 as president of the European Mission. He reorganized branches and directed food and clothing shipments to struggling Saints across the continent.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: January 14, 1946: directed distribution of about 2,500 tons of relief supplies.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: May 18-19, 1946, Rotterdam: organized distribution of relief supplies for European Saints.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: March 28, 1946: reorganized the Austrian District and oversaw food and clothing distribution.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Spring 1946: oversaw food and clothing distribution to members all over Europe.

answers.name: Poland
answers.fact: July 30-August 7, 1946: arranged food, financial help and safe exodus of German members.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: April 1946: visited Antwerp and Liege to coordinate postwar relief.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: February 15-18, 1946: visited branches in Denmark and gave radio interviews.

answers.name: Finland
answers.fact: July 16, 1946, Larsmo: rededicated Finland for the preaching of the gospel.

prompts.display_text: Pin one of the 20 largest countries by area that has a temple dedicated, under construction or announced (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: One of the 20 largest countries in the world by land area that has a temple dedicated, under construction or announced (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology; UN Statistics Division area data
prompts.summary: Thirteen of the 20 largest countries by area have a temple at some stage as of October 2026. The giants with dedicated temples include the United States, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Australia, Argentina, China (Hong Kong) and Peru; India and DR Congo are building, and Russia, Indonesia and Mongolia have announced temples.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Fifth largest; São Paulo temple (1978).

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Second largest; first temple Cardston Alberta (1923).

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Thirteenth largest; Mexico City temple (1983).

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Third largest country; more than 100 dedicated temples.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Eighth largest; Buenos Aires temple (1986).

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Sixth largest; Sydney temple (1984).

answers.name: China
answers.fact: Fourth largest; Hong Kong temple (1996), Shanghai announced.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: Seventh largest; Bengaluru temple under construction.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Nineteenth largest; Lima temple (1986).

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: Eleventh largest; Kinshasa temple (2019).

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: Largest country; a temple in Russia was announced in 2018.

answers.name: Indonesia
answers.fact: Fourteenth largest; Jakarta temple announced.

answers.name: Mongolia
answers.fact: Eighteenth largest; Ulaanbaatar temple announced.
